items.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
items.summary: This framework helps data scientists determine if using an LLM router is actually beneficial by auditing whether their model portfolio offers enough performance diversity to justify the complexity.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.summary: This method improves mathematical reasoning in LLMs by mining and diversifying reasoning steps from failed attempts, helping models find correct paths for complex problems.

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.summary: This benchmark provides a standardized way to evaluate voice agents handling complex, multi-user interactions in shared environments, which is essential for building robust conversational AI.

items.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
items.summary: The authors introduce a hybrid decision tree method that improves predictive accuracy while maintaining interpretability by using selective case-based splits instead of traditional feature-only thresholds.

items.title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory
items.summary: This paper introduces a memory system for LLM agents that prioritizes information based on its actual utility for future responses rather than just recording past conversation history.

items.summary: LoomKV enables lossless compression of KV caches for LLM serving, allowing for more efficient memory usage across GPUs and SSDs without sacrificing model output quality.

items.summary: The authors demonstrate that long-horizon agents can be effectively trained using only teacher actions, bypassing the need for proprietary chain-of-thought data from closed models.

items.summary: The researchers developed a framework to identify and mitigate human-aligned biases in LLM-based evaluators, improving the reliability of automated model assessment pipelines.

items.authors: Mathijs A. Langezaal, Egon L. van den Broek, Lukas P. A. Arts et al.

items.summary: This study compares specialized decision models against standard LLMs for multilingual emotion classification, offering data scientists a faster, more robust alternative to traditional fine-tuned encoders.

items.summary: The authors created a framework that uses AI agents to play-test and iteratively refine game designs, helping developers automate the tuning process for better player engagement.

items.summary: The researchers developed a verification mechanism for diffusion language models that identifies errors in generated text to trigger targeted regeneration, improving accuracy in complex reasoning tasks.

items.summary: The authors demonstrate that smaller, cheaper LLMs can be as effective as frontier models for heuristic discovery, proposing a bandit-based routing system to optimize cost and performance.

items.summary: This method caches LLM reasoning steps into CPU-executable code, allowing you to solve repetitive tasks much faster and cheaper without needing to re-run expensive model inference.
